_comment:
The wolf goes up the roof and down the chimney. ENTIRELY tier 1-2: whole-actor x/y/scale, a hide, sounds and an effect. It touches no part of any rig, declares no pose and needs no new art, which is why it works on ANY character against ANY prop that can be climbed. The perspective is sold by scaling DOWN as he rises - a cheat every cutout show uses, because a character who gets smaller as he goes up reads as going AWAY, and nobody has to draw a back view.

The payoff is deliberately offscreen. A splash from inside a house you cannot see into is funnier and costs nothing; animating a wolf hitting water would be tier 5.

EVERY MOVE CARRIES A DURATION. A move with none eases over the REST OF THE SHOT, so a three-step climb never finished: the wolf was still drifting up the wall when the `hide` fired at 2.68 and he vanished halfway. Multi-step travel MUST time each leg, or only the last one has room to complete.

structure._comment: Whatever house is standing here. No clip needed and no pose needed - he climbs ON it, he does not break it, so every house in the family qualifies and so will the next one.
